# Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 19 (Bi-Vb Pc19)

**ID:** Bi-Vb Pc19
**Section:** Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga (bi-vb)
**Collection:** Vinaya
**Title (Pali):** Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 19
**Title (English, from literature):** Cursing
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/vin02m1.mul7.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Paraabhisapana Sutta* (Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 19) lays down the training rule that a nun who curses herself or another incurs an offense requiring confession (*pācittiya*). The rule and its accompanying casuistry primarily regulate interpersonal interactions among members of the monastic order [Hüsken 1997]. Along with the rule immediately following it, this regulation was intended to prevent nuns from adopting worldly habits or practices from other contemporary ascetic traditions that were considered unhelpful for achieving the Buddhist goal of liberation [Hüsken 1997]. Exemption from penalty (*anāpatti*) is granted if the cursing language occurs in the context of providing an explanation, reciting canonical texts, or offering instruction [Hüsken 1997].

Within the Pali Vinaya, the rule is closely tied to its counterpart in the Bhikkhunī Pātimokkha (*pli-tv-bi-pm-pc19*) and the Bhikkhunī Parivāra. Broad parallel traditions are preserved across the Vinayas of multiple early schools, including Dharmaguptaka (Bi-Vb Pc 88), Mahīśāsaka (Bi-Vb Pc 134), Sarvāstivāda (Bi-Vb Pc 93), Mahāsaṅghika (Bi-Vb Pc 87), and Mūlasarvāstivāda (in both Chinese and Tibetan translations), as well as Sanskrit versions from the Lokottaravāda and Sarvāstivāda lineages. An English translation has been prepared by Bhikkhu Brahmali.
